paper_metadata.title: Peak Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Correlates with Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Severe Traumatic Brain Injury

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes the setting and recruitment period. However, as a retrospective study from a single department, it is prone to selection bias. The participation rate of eligible vs. non-eligible patients is not reported, making it difficult to assess if the sample is truly representative of the broader sTBI population.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: patients admitted into our department between January 2013 and January 2017 for sTBI.
items.reasoning: The source population is defined as sTBI patients at a specific neurosurgery department over a 4-year period.

items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sTBI who were treated in our department
items.reasoning: While the recruitment source is clear, the retrospective nature and lack of detail on whether recruitment was consecutive or a convenience sample introduces potential bias.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The inclusion criteria were as follows: (1) isolated head trauma; (2) an admission Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score less than 9; (3) age larger than 16; (4) time interval from injury to admission less than 24 h; (5) at least two consecutive NLRs over a period of 3 days or more.
items.reasoning: Criteria are specific, including clinical (GCS), temporal (<24h), and data-availability requirements.

items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Collected data included age, gender, time interval from injury to admission, admission GCS score, injury mechanisms, vital signs (body temperature, heart rate), blood glucose level, surgery in the frst 24 h or not
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive breakdown of baseline characteristics for the cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study excludes patients with missing data or loss to follow-up but does not quantify these exclusions. This 'complete case analysis' approach in a retrospective design can lead to attrition bias if those lost to follow-up had different prognostic profiles than those included.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (Peak NLR) is based on objective laboratory data (automated blood counters) and is clearly defined. The use of a peak value over a 12-day window is well-described, though the frequency of testing varied slightly between patients.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The NLR was calculated as the ratio of neutrophil count to lymphocyte count, and peak NLR was defned as the highest NLR during these 12 days.
items.reasoning: The definition and calculation method are explicit.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: peripheral hemogram which was evaluated using venous blood samples by an automated blood counter (XN-10, Sysmex Inc., Japan).
items.reasoning: The use of a standardized automated counter provides high reliability and limits measurement bias.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: An optimized peak NLR cutof value of 18.16 was identifed with a sensitivity of 74.3% and specifcity of 72.9% (Youden Index=0.472)
items.reasoning: The cutoff was determined using the Youden Index (data-dependent), which can lead to overestimation of effect, though the primary analysis treated NLR as a continuous variable in the logistic regression.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: For the day 1 NLR, venous blood was obtained upon admission. For the NLRs on other days, blood samples were usually collected early in the morning.
items.reasoning: The protocol for blood collection was standardized across the cohort.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: at least two consecutive NLRs over a period of 3 days or more.
items.reasoning: The inclusion criteria ensured that only patients with sufficient data points to determine a 'peak' were included.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Missing data or loss to follow-up led to the exclusion of participants.
items.reasoning: Imputation was not used; missing data resulted in exclusion.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (GOS at 1 year) is a standard, validated measure in TBI research. While the paper doesn't explicitly mention blinding of the GOS assessors to the NLR values, the objective nature of the laboratory data makes differential measurement bias unlikely.

items.evidence_snippet: Unfavorable outcome was defned as 1-year GOS score of less than 4.
items.reasoning: The outcome and the time point (1 year) are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: 1-year Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) score.
items.reasoning: GOS is a globally recognized and validated tool for TBI outcome assessment.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: On their 1-year follow-up, 257 (81.3%) patients had a GOS score of less than 4.
items.reasoning: The follow-up interval was consistent for the cohort.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses multivariable logistic regression to adjust for several key confounders (age, GCS, surgery). However, as noted in the limitations, the relationship between surgery and NLR was not fully explored, and other potential confounders (e.g., secondary infections, which significantly affect NLR) were not explicitly adjusted for in the model.
